title: fix(spec)!: the filter doors refuse the three shapes they already declared refused (#19514)
body:
Part of #19514

Clause-②: no

Three accept-set narrowings in `packages/spec`, each pulling a filter door back to what this package already declared somewhere an author's parse never reached. Direction set by objectui#9050's ruling C′, quoted untranslated: 「the differences are the protocol's to close」. Triage's rider was held: Delta 3 takes the **narrow-to-the-declared-union** arm only, and the refuse-outright arm is not in this diff.

## Re-derived line numbers (branch point `c120dbdfb8`)

The dispatch carried pointers; every one was re-measured here rather than adopted.

| what | dispatch said | measured at `c120dbdfb8` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `const isPair = …` | `view.zod.ts:614` | `view.zod.ts:614` — holds |
| `if (!isPair) return;` | `view.zod.ts:633` | `view.zod.ts:633` — holds |
| `ObjectGridPropsSchema` opens | `component.zod.ts:2661` | `component.zod.ts:**2678**` — the pointer was 17 lines short |
| `defaultFilters` | `:2661 +40` | `component.zod.ts:2717` |
| `filter` | `:2661 +33` | `component.zod.ts:2710` |
| `checkViewFilterRuleValueShape` opens | — | `view.zod.ts:602` |
| `ViewFilterRuleSchema` opens | — | `view.zod.ts:695` |

## What was measured before any edit

Every reading below is `safeParse` against `packages/spec/dist` at the branch point, resolved through the package `exports` and printed by the probe (`import.meta.resolve` reported `packages/spec/dist/ui/index.mjs` and `dist/data/index.mjs`, so no reading came from `src`).

### Delta 1 — a scalar operator carrying an ARRAY

| input | before | after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `{ field:'tags', operator:'equals', value:['a'] }` | **ACCEPT** | **REFUSE** at `value`, "requires a SCALAR value" |
| `{ field:'tags', operator:'contains', value:['a','b'] }` | **ACCEPT** | **REFUSE** at `value` |
| ENVELOPE `{ field:'a', operator:'in', value:'x' }` | REFUSE (ARRAY wording) | REFUSE, wording unchanged |
| ENVELOPE `{ field:'a', operator:'between', value:[1,2,3] }` | REFUSE (range wording) | REFUSE, wording unchanged |
| ENVELOPE `{ operator:'equals', value:'x' }` — no `field` | REFUSE at `field` | REFUSE at `field` |
| NEGATIVE `{ field:'a', operator:'equals', value:'x' }` | ACCEPT | ACCEPT |
| NEGATIVE `{ field:'a', operator:'in', value:[] }` | ACCEPT | ACCEPT |
| NEGATIVE `{ field:'a', operator:'between', value:[1,2] }` | ACCEPT | ACCEPT |
| NEGATIVE `{ field:'a', operator:'is_null', value:'' }` — the UI placeholder | ACCEPT | ACCEPT |
| NEGATIVE `{ field:'a', operator:'notIn', value:['x'] }` — alias fold | ACCEPT | ACCEPT |

⚠️ **This arm reverses a reading the code recorded.** `checkViewFilterRuleValueShape`'s own docblock listed a scalar-operator array as deliberately accepted because it *"lowers to a bare `{ field: value }` deep-equality comparand, which every backend answers"*. Re-measured at source in this tree: `parseFilterAST(['tags','equals',['a']])` yields `{ tags: ['a'] }`; that node reaches `driver-sql`'s bare field-value loop at `sql-driver.ts:15043`, which calls `assertCompilableComparand(column, '=', value, filters)`; `'='` is in that file's `SCALAR_COMPARAND_OPERATORS` (`:2611`), `isBindableComparand(['a'])` is `false` because `isAcceptedFilterComparand(['a'])` is `false` (probed: `false`, against `true` for `'a'`), and the comparand is refused with the withheld `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 envelope (`unbindableComparandError`). The old reading was the one that widened past the query path. The docblock, the changeset and the ADR-0087 entry all say so explicitly rather than quietly overwriting it.

Two carve-outs are kept and pinned: an **omitted** `value` (the key is optional) and the four **valueless** operators (`is_empty` / `is_not_empty` / `is_null` / `is_not_null`), whose value position the lowering discards and where the ObjectUI client deliberately sends a truthy placeholder.

### Delta 2 — the `icontains` comparands the conformance table declares refused

| input | door | before | after |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `{ field:'name', operator:'icontains', value:'' }` | view | **ACCEPT** | **REFUSE** at `value`, "the EMPTY STRING" |
| `{ field:'name', operator:'icontains', value:42 }` | view | **ACCEPT** | **REFUSE** at `value`, "not a string" |
| `{ name: { $icontains: '' } }` | `$` | **ACCEPT** | **REFUSE** at `name.$icontains` |
| `{ name: { $icontains: 42 } }` | `$` | **ACCEPT** | **REFUSE** at `name.$icontains` |
| `{ $and: [ { name: { $icontains: '' } } ] }` | `$` | ACCEPT | REFUSE at `$and.0.name.$icontains` |
| `{ owner: { profile: { name: { $icontains: 42 } } } }` | `$` | ACCEPT | REFUSE at `owner.profile.name.$icontains` |
| ENVELOPE `{ created: { $gt: 'last_7_days' } }` | `$` | REFUSE (bare preset) | REFUSE, wording unchanged |
| ENVELOPE `{ operator:'icontains', value:'' }` — no `field` | view | REFUSE at `field` | REFUSE at `field` |
| NEGATIVE `{ name: { $icontains: 'acme' } }` | `$` | ACCEPT | ACCEPT |
| NEGATIVE `{ field:'name', operator:'icontains', value:'acme' }` | view | ACCEPT | ACCEPT |
| NEGATIVE `{ name: { $contains: '' } }` — sibling operator, no row | `$` | ACCEPT | ACCEPT |
| NEGATIVE `{ field:'name', operator:'contains', value:42 }` — sibling operator | view | ACCEPT | ACCEPT |
| NEGATIVE `{ field:'name', operator:'icontains' }` — absent value | view | ACCEPT | ACCEPT |
| NEGATIVE `{ $and: [] }` | `$` | ACCEPT | ACCEPT |

⭐ **Derived, not hand-copied.** Both doors call `isRefusedTextComparand` and `textComparandRefusalReason` — the predicate and reason text this package already publishes for exactly these rows. Nothing transcribes the table. `filter-icontains-parse-door.test.ts` §3 drives both doors from `FILTER_TEXT_CASES` itself, so a row added to the table arrives at both doors with no edit, and a door that stopped following the table goes red naming the row it dropped. §3 also pins the other direction: every ROWS-verdict case in the table still parses, and the retired-operator rejections (`$regex` / `$options`) are left to their own door.

One asymmetry, and it is a fact about the two vocabularies rather than an extra rule: a view rule's `value` is optional, so **absence** is left unjudged there (the predicate's own docblock hands that carve-out to callers with an "absent"); the `$` dialect has no absent, so an explicit `undefined` in a comparand slot is the refused non-string shape.

### Delta 3 — `ObjectGridProps.defaultFilters`

| input | before | after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `defaultFilters: 'status = active'` | **ACCEPT** | **REFUSE** |
| `defaultFilters: 42` | **ACCEPT** | **REFUSE** |
| `defaultFilters: { status: 'active' }` | **ACCEPT** | **REFUSE**, with the conversion table and a rewrite built from the author's own keys |
| `defaultFilters: [['status','=','active']]` | **ACCEPT** | **REFUSE** at `defaultFilters.0` |
| `defaultFilters: [{ nonsense: true }]` | **ACCEPT** | **REFUSE**, per-key issues |
| NEGATIVE `defaultFilters: [{ field:'s', operator:'equals', value:'a' }]` | ACCEPT | ACCEPT |
| NEGATIVE `defaultFilters: []` | ACCEPT | ACCEPT |
| NEGATIVE absent | ACCEPT | ACCEPT |
| ENVELOPE `objectName: 42` | REFUSE at `objectName` | REFUSE at `objectName` |

The pin holds the two keys **equal shape for shape** rather than transcribing a list, so the fallback keeps tracking `filter` if that declaration moves again.

⛔ Arm (b) — refuse the key outright — is **not** in this diff, per triage's rider.

## Ablation, on this change's own pins

Four arms disabled in turn with `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (literal anchor, must hit exactly once, on-disk blob change asserted, restore proven against `HEAD`). The tests are in-package and import their subjects by relative source path, so vitest compiles `src` directly and no `dist` sits between the mutation and the assertion.

| ablation | blob before → after | tests red | totals |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| A1 scalar arm — `if (!Array.isArray(value)) return;` → `if (true) return;` | `a20636191da4` → `81e31e505fd2` | 10, named below | 10 failed / 102 passed |
| A2 view `icontains` — the call removed from the refinement | `a20636191da4` → `d244ac0b8e40` | 8 | 8 failed / 45 passed |
| A3 `$` dialect `icontains` — the arm's condition made unreachable | `c047ab9065d9` → `645a7a04f24c` | 8 | 8 failed / 39 passed |
| A4 `defaultFilters` — reverted to `z.unknown().optional()` | `9aa7c654900b` → `4b14cfe92f95` | 12 | 12 failed / 360 passed |

- **A1** reddened, in `view-filter-rule-value-shape.test.ts`: `refuses equals + array`, `refuses not_equals + array`, `refuses greater_than + array`, `prescribes the author OWN first member`, `has something to say about an EMPTY array too`, `names the two vocabularies from the exported sets`, `carries no internal tracker id`, `sweeps every unshaped operator`; plus `an ARRAY is the SHAPE arm defect` (the comparand suite) and `the rule-level narrowings reach THIS key too` (the grid pin).
- **A2** reddened the four `§2 refuses …` comparand pins, the view half of both `§3` table-driven rows, the `§2` tracker-id pin and the grid pin. `§1` — the `$` door — stayed **green**, which is the attribution.
- **A3** reddened the six `§1 refuses …` pins and the `$` half of both `§3` rows. The view half stayed green, and so did the preset envelope control, which is what says the walk was still running.
- **A4** reddened all seven refused-shape rows, the equality pin, the conversion-table pin, the fall-through pin, the rule-level pin and `component.test.ts`'s re-judged AST-tuple pin.

Every restore leg: `git hash-object` back to the `HEAD` blob (`a20636191da4…`, `c047ab9065d9…`, `9aa7c654900b…`), `git diff HEAD` empty, and `git status --porcelain` empty over the whole tree afterwards.

## Fixture triage — two pins moved, neither by rote

- `view-filter-rule-value-shape.test.ts` listed `equals + array`, `not_equals + array` and `greater_than + array` as **accepted**, with a comment reciting the reading Delta 1 reverses. Those three moved to the refused side under a describe block that names the reversal; the sweep that read "both a scalar and an array parse" became two sweeps, one per direction, both derived from the exported operator vocabularies.
- `component.test.ts`'s `defaultFilters` stays HONOURED pin parsed an ObjectQL AST tuple array. Its **subject** survives — the key is honoured, not retired — so it now parses the rule array, and the tuple array's refusal is pinned beside it.

The sweep for authored instances found none: no first-party source authors `defaultFilters` with a value (the showcase's own test pins its absence), and no authored filter in this tree carries a refused `icontains` comparand or a scalar-operator array. The `$icontains: 42` hits in `driver-memory`, `driver-sql`, `formula`, `objectql` and `service-analytics` are refusal fixtures that never reach `FilterConditionSchema`; all of those suites are green.

## Changeset — measured, not assumed

`packages/spec`'s `files[]` is `dist`, `json-schema`, `liveness`, `prompts`, `llms.txt`, `README.md`, `src/**/*.zod.ts`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `api-surface`, `spec-changes.json`. `npm pack --dry-run` lists `dist/ui/index.*` and `dist/data/index.*`, and the new refusal text is present in the built bytes (`grep -c 'requires a SCALAR value' dist/ui/index.mjs` → 1, same for the CJS twin). All three edited sources are `*.zod.ts`, so they publish twice over. ⇒ this publishes; `skip-changeset` would be false.

Level **`minor`**: a breaking accept-set narrowing, carried by the `**BREAKING**` banner plus the ADR-0087 disposition rather than by the level, under the launch-window convention `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` enforces. ⛔ Not `patch` — this is not a bug fix that leaves the accept set where it was.

`node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base origin/main` reads it back:

```
✓ check-adr-0087-registration: 1 declared-breaking changeset(s), each carrying an ADR-0087 disposition.
    .changeset/19514-…md  [BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing]  registered view-filter-rule-scalar-operator-array-refused,
    filter-icontains-comparand-refused-at-parse, object-grid-default-filters-rule-array (new here: all three)
```

The changeset declares `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — the same value as the dispatch's claim, with the direction arm added, which is the arm the gate reads breaking-ness from. The claim's line is reproduced verbatim at the top of this body.

Three `SemanticMigration` entries were added as files under `migrations/entries/semantic/` and the registry regenerated with `gen:migration-registry`; nothing was typed inside the generated markers.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` — **516 files, 15107 passed**, 1 skipped, 1 todo. `typecheck` green (test layer compiles; 53 files / 257 errors held in the shrink-only debt ledger, unchanged).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` — **15 of 15 green** after `--fix` regenerated the one it proved stale (`content/docs/references/**`, three `.mdx` files carrying the moved `.describe()` text and the narrowed `defaultFilters` type). `check:api-surface`, `check:authorable-surface`, `check:export-origins`, `check:spec-changes` and `check:upgrade-guide` are all green with **no** regeneration, which is the mechanical statement that no export and no authorable key moved.
- Consumers that parse through these schemas: `@objectstack/lint` **108 files / 4111 passed**, `@objectstack/objectql` **303 files / 5057 passed**.
- `eslint . --no-inline-config` over the whole repo: **7016 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings**.
- `MANIFEST=… check:react-declaration-parity --strict` — exit 0, no new declaration divergence vs the accepted baseline.
- Gate reconciliation: `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived **111** families for these paths; **109** were run green, and the run record was reconciled with `--ran`. The two not measured are named in the report, both refusing on a whole-workspace build prerequisite rather than on anything in this diff.

## Acceptance notes

Observations found while measuring, deliberately **not** in this PR and not filed:

- `{ field:'name', operator:'icontains' }` with **no** `value` parses, on every string operator. The conformance table writes no row about absence and the published predicate explicitly hands that carve-out to the caller, so refusing it here would be widening past the table — the boundary this change holds everywhere else. Whether a valueless `icontains` should be refused at all is a question for the table's owner, not for a door.
- `ruleArrayFilterError`'s message hard-codes the subject key as `filter`. `defaultFilters` reuses it, and its `surface` string carries the key that was actually written so the sentence stays true, but a `key` option on `RuleArrayFilterErrorOptions` would read better. Not taken here: adding an optional member to a published options type enlarges the public face, and this card is declared `Clause-②: no`.
- `packages/spec/spec-changes.json` and `docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md` carry no protocol-18 semantic entries at all — not this change's three, and not the pre-existing `element-data-source-and-object-block-filter-rule-array` either. Both gates are green, so this is how the projections are scoped today rather than staleness introduced here; recorded because the entries README describes them as projections that "have to be regenerated and committed when an entry lands", which reads as if they would move.

## ⚠️ Seat correction at 2026-09-22T23:17Z

Two cells in the re-derived line-number table above were off by one and are fixed: `filter` `:2711` → **`:2710`** and `defaultFilters` `:2718` → **`:2717`**. ⭐ Re-measured by the seat at the branch point `c120dbdfb8`: `:2710` is `filter: z.array(ViewFilterRuleSchema, {` and `:2711` its `error:` line; `:2717` is `defaultFilters: z.unknown().optional()` and `:2718` its `.describe(`. The `:2678` correction the round made — against the dispatch’s stale `:2661` — is right and stands.

⭐ **Who applies a post-hoc body fix, settled.** The round declined to PATCH this body and named the conflict instead: the seat’s dispatch allowed it, but the standing dev contract says a dev writes a PR body once at creation and never re-sends it. **The standing contract wins** — the dispatch should not have overridden it, and reporting the conflict rather than silently resolving it was the right call. The seat applies the edit, as here.

## Landing

⛔ Draft, and `Part of` rather than a closing keyword: whether the card retires is triage's call. No governed surface is touched — the diff is `packages/spec/**` plus the regenerated `content/docs/references/**` and one `.changeset/` file.
